storage.choice: embedded optional field on ViewportObservationSchema (and on ViewportPageSpecSchema), NOT a sibling file
storage.justification: The record is small and hard-bounded (<=500 names x <=200 chars), so it costs a few KB in observation.json at worst. A sibling file would need a new key in ViewportFilesSchema, whose keys are all required — adding one there would stop every historical observation.json from parsing, which is exactly the compatibility the task forbids breaking. Both new fields are .optional(); a pre-28.5B observation and a pre-28.5B PageSpec parse unchanged and report `undefined` rather than an invented empty map (proved in the suite against data/linear.app/site-observations/2026-08-25T19-23-01-716Z and site-specs/2026-08-25T20-30-27-653Z).
storage.perViewport: Desktop and mobile each keep their own record. Nothing merges, dedups or diffs them — the fixture's --brand is #112233 at 1440 and #445566 at 390 and both survive to the generated CSS.

caps.recording: Never silent. The record carries discoveredCount (names found before any cap), countCapped (true when the count cap truncated the harvest) and valueCappedCount (names dropped for an over-long value — dropped, never truncated, matching the LAYOUT_RULE_VALUE_MAX_LEN convention).

capture.nameDiscovery: same-origin document.styleSheets walked with the font-harvest's try/catch-per-sheet shape, recursing into grouping rules so a name that only appears inside an @media block is still found. A rule qualifies when any comma-separated selector part is exactly `:root` or `html` (case-insensitive for `html`).
capture.valueResolution: getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue(name) — the CASCADE is the authority, not the last rule visited, which is what makes the media-query override show up at 390 and not at 1440.
capture.relevanceChoice: ALL root custom properties are captured, including ones nothing references. 'Referenced' is not decidable at capture time — a reference can live inside opaque inline-SVG markup, a pseudo-element, or a rule that only matches after a click — so guessing would drop real values. Non-root customs (e.g. one declared on .badge) are NOT captured: they do not resolve on the document element, and emitting them on the variant wrapper would invent an inherited value the source subtree never had.
capture.subtreeMode: returns the empty record, like icons/fontUrls — a region capture is not a stylesheet observation.
capture.determinism: names sorted ascending by code point in-browser before values are read.

emission.whyNotRoot: PageRenderer renders both observed viewports into ONE document as sibling .wr-variant divs, so there is a single :root for two viewports and a per-viewport difference would be unrepresentable. Custom properties inherit, so declaring them on the variant wrapper reaches that subtree and only that subtree.
emission.dedup: none — desktop and mobile each get their own block even when identical. A merge layer would be the first place a per-viewport difference could quietly disappear.
emission.ordering: scopes sorted pageId -> viewportId, declarations sorted by property name (generateLayoutCss conventions). Emitting twice is byte-identical.
emission.safety: values go through the existing isSafeCssValue; names through /^--[-A-Za-z0-9_]*$/ (case PRESERVED — nothing is lowercased, --Brand and --brand are different properties); pageId/viewportId through /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/ before they reach a selector string. Every rejection is counted (rejectedNames / rejectedValues / rejectedScopes), never silent.
emission.placement: first in the generated stylesheet, before the computed-style classes, so every rule below and every var() surviving inside captured inline-SVG markup resolves against it.

risks: Root-selector discovery is deliberately narrow: only selector parts that are exactly `:root` or `html`. A site declaring its variables on `:root:where(...)`, `html.dark`, `body`, or `*` contributes no NAME, so nothing is emitted for it even though getComputedStyle would have resolved a value. This is a discovery gap, not a wrong value — it under-reports, never invents. Widening it is a follow-up decision, not a bug fix.

Values are read at the observed viewport only. A custom property whose value depends on something other than width (hover, prefers-color-scheme, a class the page toggles) is captured in the state the observer saw, exactly like every other computed value in the pipeline.

Emission is scoped to the .wr-variant wrapper. Anything rendered OUTSIDE that wrapper (portals mounted on document.body by the interaction runtime, if any ever are) would not inherit these variables. Not observed in this fixture; worth a check if a future portal escapes the wrapper.

No manifest counter was added for customProperties — the plan carries the GeneratedCustomProperties record but generate-app does not surface blockCount/declarationCount in the manifest. Additive follow-up if the release gate wants it.

correction2.title: Reference-driven custom-property discovery — the channel no sheet walk can reach
correction2.why: correction 1 took linear.app from 0 to 135 names, but the 16 distinct names its 239 inline SVGs reference through 183 var() calls are declared ONLY in cross-origin sheets (cssRules throws), so name discovery could never see them and the 28.5A consumer defect this change exists for would have shipped at 0/16.
correction2.mechanism: during the DOM walk the collector now keeps the live <svg> roots behind inlineSvgs (same index, document order). After the sheet harvest, every `var(--name)` token is extracted from each captured SVG's outerHTML with /var\(\s*(--[-A-Za-z0-9_]+)/g (case PRESERVED, never lowercased) and each name is resolved at the CONSUMING element via getComputedStyle(svgRoot).getPropertyValue(name) — the value the source paint actually used. Resolved names are merged into the SAME per-viewport record, re-sorted by code point, and emitted on the variant wrapper, from which they inherit down to the same consumers in the clone.
correction2.precedenceRule: SHEET WINS. A name already discovered from a stylesheet keeps its sheet/root-resolved value and is not element-resolved at all. Rationale: the sheet channel is the one whose scope is PROVEN root-level, so its value is the honest one to declare on a wrapper standing in for :root; element resolution exists only to reach names no readable sheet revealed. The overlap is never silent — it is counted in referenceSheetKnownCount (linear: 0; fixture 1: 1).
correction2.conflictRule: FIRST CONSUMING ELEMENT IN DOCUMENT ORDER WINS. The walk is depth-first from documentElement, so 'first' is a function of the page, not of timing. Every later element resolving the same name to a DIFFERENT non-empty value increments referenceResolutionConflicts — wrapper-level emission can carry only one value per name, so that counter is the honesty channel for the value that was not carried. linear: 0 conflicts.
correction2.unresolvedRule: a referenced name is only counted unresolved once EVERY consuming element resolved it to "" (a later consumer can still resolve what the first could not). Counted in its own referenceUnresolvedCount rather than the sheet channel's unresolvedCount, so the two discovery channels stay separately diagnosable. Reference names dropped by the value cap fold into the shared valueCappedCount (same drop-never-truncate convention); reference names dropped by the count cap set countCapped.
correction2.scope: INLINE SVG MARKUP ONLY. var() references living in element `style` attributes, in pseudo-element content, or in observed computed values are NOT harvested — inline SVG is the proven 28.5A consumer and the only channel measured. Widening it stays a separate, separately-measured decision. Documented in collect-dom.ts.
